questions.question: What is defensive driving?

options.text: Spotting dangerous situations and taking action to avoid accidents.
Protecting yourself from bad drivers by passing them in traffic.
Staying very close to the vehicle in front of you.
Changing lanes quickly to move through traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Spotting dangerous situations and taking action to avoid accidents.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means spotting dangerous situations and acting before an accident happens. It helps you avoid problems with aggressive, reckless, careless, or impaired drivers and pedestrians.

questions.question: A pedestrian starts to cross in front of your vehicle. What should you do?

options.text: Flash your lights.
Slow down.
Speed up and pass in front of the pedestrian.
Stop and let the pedestrian cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let the pedestrian cross.
questions.explanation: Slow down and prepare to stop whenever you see pedestrians on or crossing the road. Be extra careful near children. Always give pedestrians the right-of-way in a crosswalk.

questions.question: It starts to sleet or snow while you are driving. What should you do?

options.text: Keep your windshield and mirrors clear.
Leave more space between your vehicle and the ones you are following.
Drive carefully around all other vehicles.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: In snow, keep your windshield and mirrors clear. Increase your following distance in wet, cold weather because slippery roads need more distance for your vehicle to stop.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Sharp right turn.
A road joins from the right.
The road ahead turns sharply right, then sharply left.
Winding road ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road ahead turns sharply right, then sharply left.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road ahead turns sharply to the right and then sharply to the left.

questions.question: When is it illegal to drive below the speed limit?

options.text: When slow driving blocks the normal flow of traffic.
When in heavy traffic in a construction zone.
Only when driving in rural areas.
When driving in bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: When slow driving blocks the normal flow of traffic.
questions.explanation: It is illegal to drive so slowly that you block normal traffic flow. You can get a ticket for driving too slowly.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You cannot exit the freeway.
You can continue through or exit the freeway from your current lane.
You can stay in your lane and continue through the interchange.
You must exit the freeway if you stay in your current lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must exit the freeway if you stay in your current lane.
questions.explanation: An "Exit only" sign means your lane will leave the freeway and form a ramp. If you are in a lane under an "Exit only" sign, you can change lanes to go through the interchange, or you must exit the highway.

questions.question: You see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights. What must you do?

options.text: Slow down and stay in your lane.
Keep driving in your lane.
Pull to the right curb and stop.
Stop exactly where you are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the right curb and stop.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights or hear a siren, pull to the curb or edge of the road right away and stop.

questions.question: Where can you take the Missouri driver test?

options.text: Any Missouri State Highway Patrol testing station.
Any Department of Transportation office.
Any Missouri contract office.
The nearest high school driver education class.

questions.correctAnswerText: Any Missouri State Highway Patrol testing station.
questions.explanation: The Missouri State Highway Patrol gives the driver test. Contact the State Highway Patrol or Department of Revenue to find the testing center nearest you.

questions.question: How can you avoid hitting vehicles in your blind spots?

options.text: Turn your head quickly to check your blind spot before changing lanes.
Adjust your rearview mirrors every few minutes.
Honk your horn right before turning or changing lanes.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head quickly to check your blind spot before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Before turning or changing lanes, turn your head and look over your shoulder in the direction you are moving to check your blind spot. Do not rely on mirrors alone.

questions.question: Can you drive around or under a gate that is being lowered or raised at a railroad crossing?

options.text: Yes, as long as a train is not too close.
Yes, if your vehicle can do so without damaging the gate.
Yes, if you look carefully in both directions.
No, never.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, never.
questions.explanation: Flashing red lights, lowered crossing gates, and bells at a railroad crossing mean you must stop completely. Do not cross the tracks until the lights and bells stop and the gates are fully raised. Never drive around or under a gate that is moving.

questions.question: The space you need to cross traffic depends on:

options.text: Road conditions, weather, and oncoming traffic.
The presence of a stop sign.
Using your turn signals.
Cars behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Road conditions, weather, and oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: The space you need to cross traffic depends on road conditions, weather, and oncoming traffic.

questions.question: At a light rail intersection, you should always:

options.text: Look both ways before crossing the tracks.
Pay attention and obey all traffic signals.
Share the road with pedestrians and bicyclists.
All of these.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of these.
questions.explanation: Never drive around lowered crossing gates. Always look both ways before crossing train tracks and obey all signs and traffic signals. Trains share the road with cars and bicyclists.

questions.question: What does SATOP stand for?

options.text: Substance Abuse Traffic Offender Program.
Salt And Tar On Pavement.
Steer At The Other Point.
Stop Airing Tires Over Pressure.

questions.correctAnswerText: Substance Abuse Traffic Offender Program.
questions.explanation: SATOP stands for Substance Abuse Traffic Offender Program. People convicted of alcohol-related driving offenses must complete this program.

questions.question: What should you do if your accelerator sticks while driving?

options.text: Reach down and try to pull it up.
Shift to park.
Shift to neutral and press the brake firmly.
Turn off the engine.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift to neutral and press the brake firmly.
questions.explanation: If your accelerator sticks, keep your eyes on the road. Quickly shift to neutral and press the brake firmly. When safe, pull off the road and turn off the engine.

questions.question: At dusk or on overcast days, you should:

options.text: Drive with your four-way flashers on.
Drive with your parking lights on.
Not turn on any lights.
Turn on your headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your headlights.
questions.explanation: Turn on your headlights at dusk and on overcast days. Use low beams when within 1,000 feet of oncoming traffic or 500 feet of the car ahead. Always use low beams in poor weather.

questions.question: Drive below the posted speed limit when:

options.text: Anything makes conditions less than perfect.
You see a police car.
You are entering a highway with other cars.
You are on a four-lane road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Anything makes conditions less than perfect.
questions.explanation: When the road is wet or slippery, when visibility is poor, or when anything else makes conditions less than perfect, drive below the speed limit. You can be ticketed for speeding even if you are within the posted limit.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You must turn left or right.
You are approaching a T intersection.
Your road meets a divided highway.
You are on an overpass over a divided highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your road meets a divided highway.
questions.explanation: This sign means your road meets a divided highway. A divided highway has two one-way roads separated by a median or guide rail.

questions.question: You are approaching a railroad crossing with a standard crossbuck but no gates or lights. You should:

options.text: Cross with extreme caution only when you know no train is coming.
Turn down your radio to listen for a train.
Wait for a flagger's signal if one is present.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Approach all railroad crossings with extreme caution and cross only when you are sure no train is coming from either direction. If a flagger is present, follow their instructions.

questions.question: A red circle with a slash through the middle on a sign means:

options.text: Come to a complete stop.
An action is forbidden.
Some drivers should yield to others.
Drive under the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: An action is forbidden.
questions.explanation: A red circle with a slash means an action is forbidden. These signs are rectangular, white, and have red and black markings.

questions.question: What does a single dashed yellow line between traffic mean?

options.text: Drivers may pass if it is safe.
Both lanes go in the same direction.
Drivers may not pass.
Drivers may pass even if it is dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers may pass if it is safe.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic going in opposite directions. A single dashed yellow line means drivers in both directions may pass. You can only pass if you will not interfere with oncoming traffic.

questions.question: How should you let others know you want to be an organ donor?

options.text: Fill out the organ donor section on the back of your license.
Tell your family about your decision.
Have two witnesses sign the back of your license.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: To register as an organ donor, complete the back of your license, tell your family, and sign up online or in person when you apply for or renew your license.

questions.question: When should you increase the distance between your car and the car ahead?

options.text: When driving behind a large vehicle that blocks your view.
When exiting an expressway.
When following a motorcycle.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when behind a large vehicle blocking your view, in bad weather, in heavy traffic, when exiting an expressway, when behind a motorcycle or bicycle, or when someone is tailgating you.

questions.question: When turning right on a green light, you must:

options.text: Keep your normal speed.
Stop and look for police cars.
Let pedestrians go first.
Drive faster than normal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let pedestrians go first.
questions.explanation: You can turn right or left at a green light unless a sign says otherwise. When turning, you must let other vehicles and pedestrians in the intersection go first.

questions.question: When can you cross a dashed white line?

options.text: Anytime.
Only during the day.
When it is safe to change lanes.
Only when passing a motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: When it is safe to change lanes.
questions.explanation: Dashed white lines separate traffic lanes going in the same direction. You can cross dashed lines to pass if it is safe.

questions.question: It starts to rain while you are driving. What should you do?

options.text: Drive faster than the traffic around you.
Drive at the posted speed limit.
Slow down.
Drive very close to the vehicle ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: When rain makes it hard to see, slow down and turn on your headlights. If rain is very heavy and you cannot see clearly, pull to the shoulder and stop until it improves.
